title: Capstone: multiply on your own CPU
task: Set `PROGRAM` to an assembly program that multiplies the numbers at `X` and `Y` and leaves the product at `RESULT`, using only the 8 instructions (there's no multiply). It must set `RESULT` to 0 itself, handle `Y = 0`, and `HALT` when it's done.
hints: Re-read "Translating a loop to assembly" next to the Python loop above it: each Python line becomes one to three instructions. Every operand is an address, so the constants 0 and 1 need their own `DATA` words.

The shape: set RESULT to 0 by loading from a `ZERO: DATA 0` word. Then `LOOP:` loads Y and does `JZ DONE`. The body adds X into RESULT (load, add, store), then counts Y down by subtracting a `ONE: DATA 1` word, and ends with `JMP LOOP`. `DONE: HALT` comes next, then five data words: X, Y, RESULT, ZERO and ONE.
The whole program: `LOAD ZERO`, `STORE RESULT`, `LOOP: LOAD Y`, `JZ DONE`, `LOAD RESULT`, `ADD X`, `STORE RESULT`, `LOAD Y`, `SUB ONE`, `STORE Y`, `JMP LOOP`, `DONE: HALT`, then the data words.

quiz.q: With this loop, how many times does `result = result + x` run when x = 4 and y = 0?
quiz.why: The check comes first: y is already 0, so the body never runs and the result stays 0.

quiz.q: Trace x = 4, y = 3. At the 4th check of Y, what is RESULT?
quiz.why: Each pass adds 4: RESULT is 0, 4, 8, 12 at the 1st to 4th checks. At the 4th, Y is 0 and the loop ends.

review.q: How many instructions does `RESULT = RESULT + X` take in this machine's assembly?
review.why: `LOAD RESULT`, `ADD X`, `STORE RESULT`: the accumulator is the only place arithmetic happens.

review.q: Why does the multiply program need a `ZERO: DATA 0` word?

options.text: So the program is exactly 32 words long
options.why: The assembler pads with zeros on its own. The program can be any length up to 32.

options.text: Every operand is an address, so to put 0 in the accumulator you load it from a word that holds 0
options.why: There's no "load the number 0" instruction. And RESULT can start as junk, so the program has to clear it.

options.text: `HALT` reads it to know when to stop
options.why: `HALT` takes no operand. It stops the CPU as soon as it runs.

review.q: With the lesson's multiply program, how many steps does 5 × 0 take, counting the HALT?
review.why: `LOAD ZERO`, `STORE RESULT`, `LOAD Y`, `JZ DONE`, `HALT`: Y is 0, so the loop body never runs.
